related_questions.question: What is the most accurate test for COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: The most accurate test for COVID-19 is generally considered to be the molecular test, often referred to as a PCR test. These tests are highly sensitive and specific, meaning they can reliably detect even small amounts of the virus and are less likely to produce false positive or false negative results.
snippet_highlighted_words: molecular test, often referred to as a PCR test

text_blocks.snippet: Here's why PCR tests are considered the most accurate:

list.title: Detects viral genetic material:
list.snippet: PCR tests work by detecting the specific genetic material of the virus, making them highly specific and less likely to be affected by other viruses or substances in the sample.

list.title: Laboratory processing:
list.snippet: PCR tests typically involve processing in a laboratory, which allows for more controlled and reliable results.

list.title: High sensitivity:
list.snippet: PCR tests are highly sensitive, meaning they can detect even very low levels of the virus, which is important for early detection and preventing further spread, according to OSF HealthCare.

text_blocks.snippet: While antigen tests, also known as "rapid tests," are more convenient and offer faster results, they are generally less accurate than PCR tests, according to Yale Medicine.
